land.text: England and Wales, the larger part of the union: Cliopatria's Kingdom of England row runs to 1708

predecessors.note: Cliopatria's England row ends 1708 and its Great Britain row begins 1709; the union took effect on 1 May 1707 (Kingdom of Great Britain page).

land.text: the Kingdom of Scotland, united with England by the Acts of Union 1707

predecessors.note: Cliopatria's Kingdom of Scotland row ends in 1608; the Scottish land enters Great Britain in 1707.

land.text: 'Great Britain was merged into the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland on 1 January 1801'

successors.note: The Kingdom of Ireland (kingdom-of-ireland) joins in the same act; see the united-kingdom dossier.

rulers.name: Anne
rulers.note: The List of British monarchs table gives 1 May 1707 to 1 August 1714 for Great Britain; the body text dates her accession to 8 March 1702 as Queen of England and Scotland.

rulers.name: George I
rulers.note: 1 August 1714 to 11 June 1727 (List of British monarchs).

rulers.name: George II
rulers.note: 11 June 1727 to 25 October 1760 (List of British monarchs).

rulers.name: George III
rulers.note: From 25 October 1760; he continues as King of the United Kingdom to 29 January 1820 (List of British monarchs).

correction.text: Great Britain as one kingdom from 1 May 1707: the Cliopatria 1709 land (Great Britain, the Hebrides and Northern Isles, the Isle of Man) without Ireland, which 'remained formally separate, with its own parliament'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's Great Britain row begins in 1709 and its Kingdom of England row runs to 1708, so 1707 and 1708 would be drawn as England and Scotland. The page: 'The state was created by the 1706 Treaty of Union and ratified by the Acts of Union 1707'; 'The Acts came into effect on 1 May 1707'. Drawn as Cliopatria's 1709 land without Ireland (see _1709).

correction.text: the Cliopatria 1709 land without Ireland: Great Britain, the Hebrides and Northern Isles and the Isle of Man 'in the king's domain'

keyframe_review.note: 341,693 km2 (shapes.csv) against no area on the page; the United Kingdom infobox (244,376 km2, no year) plus the Irish Free State infobox (70,000 km2, no year) make 314,376 km2, ratio 1.09, so the size is right but the shape holds Ireland. The page: 'in legislative and personal union with the Kingdom of Ireland from its inception' and 'Ireland remained formally separate, with its own parliament, until the Acts of Union 1800'. Ireland is therefore taken out of the direct land and drawn as a vassal tint (ledger 1707), matching the kingdom-of-ireland dossier. The page excludes the Isle of Man and the Channel Islands from the union ('with the exception of the Isle of Man and the Channel Islands'; 'in the king's domain'); the 2 Manx cells are left in as the king's domain. Gibraltar (1713) and Menorca (1708/1713) enter by ledger events; Cliopatria draws neither before 1794 (Gibraltar) or 1799 (Menorca).

correction.text: the Cliopatria 1757 land without Ireland, with Gibraltar: 'control of Menorca and Gibraltar; it retains the latter territory to this day'

keyframe_review.note: 341,650 km2: the same land as _1709 (43 km2 smaller, the difference of single boundary cells). Adjusted as _1709, and Gibraltar is added because Spain ceded it in 1713 ('In Article X, Spain ceded the strategic ports of Gibraltar and Menorca'; Britain 'retains the latter territory to this day'); Cliopatria draws Gibraltar only from 1794. Menorca is not in this baseline: French forces took it in 1756 (Menorca page), and the ledger returns it in 1763.

correction.text: the Cliopatria 1762 land without Ireland, with Gibraltar (Utrecht, 1713)

keyframe_review.note: 341,693 km2, identical in size to _1709. Adjusted as _1757: Ireland out (vassal tint), Gibraltar in. Menorca is returned by the 1763 Treaty of Paris and lost again in 1782 (ledger events, Menorca page).

correction.text: the Cliopatria 1794 land without Ireland and without Corsica ('Personal union with Great Britain'): Great Britain, the Isle of Man and Gibraltar

keyframe_review.note: 353,085 km2: the 1762 land plus 34 cells in Corsica (about 8,700 km2) and the cell of Gibraltar. The Corsican cells are the Anglo-Corsican Kingdom: 'Status: Personal union with Great Britain', 'a client state of the Kingdom of Great Britain', established 15-19 June 1794. A client is a vassal tint, not direct land, so Corsica is taken out (ledger: vassal_start June 1794) and Ireland as before; Gibraltar stays. The page gives no area.

correction.text: the Cliopatria 1796 land without Ireland and without Corsica (client to 11 October 1796)

keyframe_review.note: 353,042 km2, the same land as _1794. Corsica is a client until the British evacuation on 11 October 1796 ('British evacuation: 11 October 1796'; 'Conquered: 19 October 1796'), so the year is a client year to October. Adjusted as _1794.

correction.text: the Cliopatria 1797 land without Ireland and without Elba: Great Britain, the Isle of Man and Gibraltar

keyframe_review.note: 342,322 km2: Corsica is gone and two cells appear at Elba (about 530 km2). The Elba page: 'The British landed on the island of Elba in 1796' to protect French royalists at Portoferraio; it does not say when they left ('In 1801, the Peace of Luneville gave Elba to the Kingdom of Etruria'). Elba is an occupation of someone else's land, so it is taken out of the direct shape (ledger: occupation 1796-1800); Ireland as before.

correction.text: the Cliopatria 1799 land without Ireland and without Elba: Great Britain, the Isle of Man, Gibraltar and Menorca 'captured ... in 1798'

keyframe_review.note: 343,316 km2: the 1797 land plus 2 cells at Menorca (about 510 km2). 'The British once again captured Menorca in 1798 during the French Revolutionary Wars' (ledger 1798, gain), so Menorca stays. Elba and Ireland are taken out as in _1797.

correction.text: the Cliopatria 1800 land without Ireland: Great Britain, the Isle of Man, Gibraltar, Menorca and Malta

keyframe_review.note: 343,293 km2 for 1800-1819; for this dossier only 1800 counts (the United Kingdom dossier takes 1801-1819). Elba drops out and Malta enters: the French garrison 'finally surrendered on 4 September 1800' and Malta is a 'Protectorate of the United Kingdom'. Malta and Menorca stay; Ireland is taken out as a vassal tint until the union of 1 January 1801.

region.text: England (with Wales) and Scotland, which together form Great Britain

ledger.note: 1707: England and Scotland unite as the Kingdom of Great Britain. UK page: 'On 1 May 1707 the Kingdom of Great Britain was formed' and 'Acts of Union of England and Scotland: 1 May 1707'; Kingdom of Great Britain page: 'The Acts came into effect on 1 May 1707' after the 'Treaty of Union: 22 July 1706'. The Scottish share is kingdom-of-scotland (predecessors).

region.text: the island of Ireland: 'the Kingdom of Ireland', 'formally separate, with its own parliament'

ledger.note: 1707: Ireland stays a separate kingdom, dependent on the new Britain. 'The resulting kingdom was in legislative and personal union with the Kingdom of Ireland from its inception'; 'the Parliament of Ireland was subordinate to the Parliament of England ... and after 1707 to the Parliament of Great Britain'; the Declaratory Act 1719 declared the Kingdom of Ireland 'subordinate to and dependent upon the crown of Great Britain'. The repeal in 1782 and the 'Irish constitution of 1782' gave 'a period of legislative freedom' but not an end to the union of crowns, so the tint runs to 1800. Cliopatria draws Ireland as direct British land.
1708: Anglo-Dutch forces take Menorca from Spain. 'Anglo-Dutch forces captured Menorca in 1708 during the War of the Spanish Succession.' Hatched until the cession of 1713.
1713: the occupation of Menorca ends in formal cession (next event).

region.text: Menorca, 'ceded to Great Britain by Spain in the 1713 Peace of Utrecht'

ledger.note: 1713: Spain cedes Menorca to Great Britain. 'was formally ceded to Great Britain by Spain in the 1713 Peace of Utrecht'; 'during the period of British rule Menorca's capital was moved to Mahon'. The Utrecht page dates the Anglo-Spanish treaty to 13 July.

region.text: Gibraltar: 'the strategic ports of Gibraltar and Menorca'

ledger.note: 1713: Spain cedes Gibraltar to Great Britain at Utrecht. 'In Article X, Spain ceded the strategic ports of Gibraltar and Menorca'; 'Spain under Philip V signed separate peace treaties with Savoy and Great Britain at Utrecht on 13 July' (the sentence has no year; the page's surrounding text puts the main treaties on 11 April 1713); Britain gained 'control of Menorca and Gibraltar; it retains the latter territory to this day'. The page does not date the 1704 capture.
1756: France takes Menorca. 'Menorca remained a British possession until 1756, when French forces captured it.' The Kingdom of Great Britain page: 'Britain lost the island of Minorca in 1756'.
1763: Menorca returns to Britain by the Treaty of Paris. 'led the island to be ceded back to them in the 1763 Treaty of Paris'.

1782: Franco-Spanish forces take Menorca. 'In 1782, Franco-Spanish forces captured the island during the American Revolutionary War'; 'Britain ceded the island back to Spain in the 1783 Peace of Paris'.

region.text: Corsica, where the page records 'Siege of Calvi: 17 June - 10 August 1794'

ledger.note: 1794: British forces begin the siege of Calvi. Infobox 'Siege of Calvi: 17 June - 10 August 1794'. The first British campaign that holds ground in Corsica; the page does not say who held Calvi, so the French First Republic as counterpart is the researcher's reading of 'Corsica's secession from France' declared at Corte in 1793.

region.text: Corsica: the Anglo-Corsican Kingdom, 'a client state of the Kingdom of Great Britain'

ledger.note: 1794: Corsica becomes the Anglo-Corsican Kingdom under the British crown. Infobox 'Established: 15-19 June 1794'; 'Status: Personal union with Great Britain'; the lead calls it 'a client state of the Kingdom of Great Britain'; 'Viceroy: Sir Gilbert Elliot'; capital 'Corte (until 1795) Bastia (from 1795)'.
10 August 1794: the siege of Calvi ends (infobox 'Siege of Calvi: 17 June - 10 August 1794'); the page does not name Calvi's fall in words, so the end is the siege's end date.

1796: British forces land on Elba. 'The British landed on the island of Elba in 1796' 'to protect the 4,000 French royalists who had found asylum in Portoferraio two years earlier.' The page does not name the power the island belonged to.

11 October 1796: the British evacuate Corsica. Infobox 'British evacuation: 11 October 1796'; 'Conquered: 19 October 1796'; 'With Spain coming in on the side of the French' the British 'realised their position in the Mediterranean was precarious'. The land returns to France (french-directory).
1798: Britain retakes Menorca. 'The British once again captured Menorca in 1798 during the French Revolutionary Wars.' The Treaty of Amiens return to Spain in 1802 is in the united-kingdom dossier.

1800: Elba leaves British hands (page silent). The page gives only the 1796 landing and 'In 1801, the Peace of Luneville gave Elba to the Kingdom of Etruria'; the year 1800 is Cliopatria's (its shape drops the Elba cells in 1800).

region.text: the Maltese Islands, 'Protectorate of the United Kingdom'

ledger.note: 4 September 1800: the French garrison surrenders and Malta passes to Britain as a protectorate. The French garrison under General Vaubois 'finally surrendered on 4 September 1800'; infobox 'Status: Protectorate of the United Kingdom'; 'the transformation of the islands to the Crown Colony of Malta in 1813'; 'Malta officially became a colony by the Treaty of Paris in 1814'. French rule is the french-consulate row in this year.

31 December 1800: the Kingdom of Ireland ends its separate existence. Infobox 'Union with Ireland: 31 December 1800'; 'Ireland remained formally separate, with its own parliament, until the Acts of Union 1800 took effect'. Ireland joins the new United Kingdom directly (united-kingdom ledger 1801).

region.text: Great Britain, the Isle of Man, Gibraltar, Menorca and Malta

ledger.note: 31 December 1800: Great Britain ends. 'Great Britain was merged into the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland on 1 January 1801'; the state existed 'from 1707 ... to the end of 1800'. Its land, with Ireland, is the United Kingdom.

wars.name: War of the Spanish Succession
wars.outcome: British gains at Utrecht: 'From France, Great Britain gained Newfoundland and Acadia, and from Spain Gibraltar and Menorca.' Menorca had been taken in 1708 and Gibraltar is held 'to this day'.
wars.note: The page gives the war as 1702-14 ('During the War of the Spanish Succession (1702-14) England continued its policy of forming and funding alliances'); the Utrecht page and the Menorca page date the cessions.

wars.name: Jacobite risings
wars.outcome: No border moved: the rising of 1715 'based in Scotland' and the cause of the Stuarts 'ended in defeat ... in 1746'.
wars.note: The 1745 rising is not named on the page; only 1715 and the defeat of 1746.

wars.name: Seven Years' War
wars.outcome: Menorca was lost in 1756 and 'ceded back to them in the 1763 Treaty of Paris'; the Treaty of Paris of 1763 'marked the high point of the First British Empire' (Kingdom of Great Britain page).
wars.note: The Kingdom of Great Britain page: 'The Seven Years' War, which began in 1756'.

wars.name: American Revolutionary War
wars.outcome: Menorca was captured in 1782 and ceded to Spain by the 1783 Peace of Paris; the colonies are the American dossiers' matter.
wars.note: The page: 'The American war of independence, which lasted from 1775 to 1783'; Menorca facts from the Menorca page ('In 1782, Franco-Spanish forces captured the island').

wars.name: French Revolutionary Wars
wars.outcome: Britain held Corsica as a client (June 1794 - 11 October 1796), landed on Elba (1796), retook Menorca (1798) and took Malta (4 September 1800).
wars.note: The Kingdom of Great Britain page says only that 'Britain was a leading belligerent in the French Revolutionary Wars' and 'The long bitter wars with France 1793-1815'; the span to 1802 is the Menorca page's Treaty of Amiens year.

certainty.note: The coast of Great Britain and the Anglo-Scottish line are long fixed; the outposts (Gibraltar by the Utrecht cession, Menorca, Malta) are small enclaves. The occupations (Menorca 1708-13, Elba 1796-1800) and the Corsican client are tints, not borders.

notes: Written for batch eu-11-l from eight pages: six of its own (Kingdom of Great Britain, Treaty of Utrecht, Anglo-Corsican Kingdom, Elba, Menorca, Malta Protectorate; budget up to 5 for the 9 keyframes reviewed, so one over) and two shared with the united-kingdom dossier (United Kingdom, List of British monarchs). Cliopatria's Kingdom of Great Britain row runs 1709-2024 and is split here: this dossier is Great Britain 1707-1800, united-kingdom takes 1801 onward (new slug, written in the same batch). IDENTITY: Cliopatria's Wikipedia field is 'Great Britain' (the island) and its Wikidata id Q23666 is the island's; the state's own article is 'Kingdom of Great Britain', used here. The id is kept as Cliopatria gives it. IRELAND: Cliopatria draws the whole island as direct Great Britain from 1709. The kingdom-of-ireland dossier (another part) types Ireland a colony and asks the Great Britain dossier to subtract it; every keyframe here takes Ireland out and the ledger holds it as a vassal tint 1707-1800. CLIOPATRIA FRAGMENTS: 1794-1796 Corsica (34 cells) and Gibraltar (1 cell); 1797-1799 two cells at Elba; 1799 two cells at Menorca; 1800 one cell at Malta. Gibraltar was ceded in 1713 but is drawn only from 1794; Menorca was British 1708-1756, 1763-1782 and 1798-1802 but is drawn only 1799-1800; both are corrected through ledger events, with Gibraltar in the baseline of the 1757 and 1762 keyframes. NOT SETTLED: the 1704 capture of Gibraltar and the date the British left Elba (the Elba page is silent; the 1800 end is Cliopatria's, confidence 1). Mahon as the capital of Menorca (1722) is on the Menorca page but moves no border. The Isle of Man (Cliopatria draws 2 cells) is kept as 'the king's domain'; the Channel Islands are not drawn. Hanover (personal union 1714-1837) is not drawn here: Cliopatria adds it only in 1820 (see united-kingdom). Pages that failed: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_Menorca (url_not_found, replaced by Menorca). Counterparts needing dossiers: anglo-corsican-kingdom (1794-1796), written in this batch from the Anglo-Corsican page. Region names the gazetteer lacks: Menorca (used as a 40 km radius at 4.1 E 40.0 N), Elba (20 km at 10.3 E 42.78 N).
